items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: the first trumpet player was Carl George... And while we were there it was Ernie Royal, Joe Newman and I were the trumpets. And then when Carl came back they decided to keep four trumpets.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you about when you were with the couple of big bands before the Marines, and then after again, can you recall if you had a goal? An eventual goal for your music career at that point?

You know I was so thrilled in a way and surprised too that I ended up for instance in Les Hite’s band because I was 19 years old and this was quite an experience for me, and I remember when I left Philadelphia on a bus to go to Lansing, Michigan to join Les Hite’s band and my mother accompanied me to the bus terminal, and I can remember my mother standing, as I had the window down and the bus is loaded with people, and my mother saying, “don’t you do anything to embarrass this family while you’re away.” And I…

rather surprised and I was actually in awe of most of the fellows who were in those bands. They were a little older than me. Some of them were in my age group but a lot of them were older and had a lot more experience. So I felt kind of lucky to be there. When I left Les Hite I joined the Lionel Hampton band, which at that time was roaring, and I was really in awe of that band. I mean I was again quite happy that I became a member. But it’s strange because the first trumpet player was Carl George and he was…
